title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan: Putting Lapsed Cover Back into Force
content:
Cover that has fallen away is put back into force on a charge the host carries, and cover then runs again from the day the restoration is recorded. The restoration is made on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment whose cover fell away, and the charge is booked to what the host owes on that enrolment.

### Situation of use and capability

`restore_protection_cover_3adbf459` moves the enrolment back to active, clears the ground that was recorded against it, sets the day cover starts running again to today, and books the charge for restoring it to what the host owes on the enrolment. The host can afterwards see the enrolment live again from today with that charge added to what they owe.

### How it is invoked

The tool is unlocked and then called by the desk agent, who works out the charge and passes it in.

### Parameters

- `enrollment_id` — the reference number of the host protection enrolment being put back into force, read from the enrolment record retrieved for this host.
- `restoration_charge_amount` — the charge for putting the cover back into force, in USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half-up to the cent; zero is accepted and means nothing is charged for the restoration.

### Return

A confirmation line in plain text carrying the enrolment reference, the day cover starts running again as YYYY-MM-DD, the charge booked in USD to the cent and the enrolment's new amount owed by the host. Receiving that line means the enrolment is active again; no other output is produced.
